summary: Reviewed every unique manifest sky/backdrop and all 15 atmosphere PNG sources through source images, scene presets and dark/light/crop QA. 27 assets: 23 approved, 3 replace, 1 inactive. Batch-03 reuses the approved batch-02 misty sky and adds no unique backdrop.

items.reason: Soft painted trees and depth are compatible, but the cream sunlit sky, mint haze and golden foliage read as a pastoral storybook plate beside the subdued batch-05/06 regional skies. Repaint the daylight variant with overcast pewter sky, muted olive foliage and restrained warm breaks while preserving its valley layout.
Muted gray-green forest, layered mist and softened distant ridges match the atmospheric painterly family. The overcast palette is intentional.
Moonlit slate-blue values and layered valley haze preserve the same painted forest language. Moon and cloud edges provide justified night contrast without neon color.

Tiny irregular neutral flecks are non-emissive and unobtrusive in dark/light QA and the warm preset; appropriate subdued ash.
Sparse fine gray-blue slanted streaks remain low contrast on dark and light QA backgrounds; reads as rain rather than UI decoration.
Small varied gray-white dots remain soft and restrained in scene and dark/light QA; simple shapes suit a moving weather field.
Soft low-opacity neutral field gives broad diffuse haze in the fog/swamp presets; no hard graphic contour or neon cast. Crop QA supports the same understated field.

Disabled by default in the manifest. Source visually shows dense cloudlike white rolls with hard extracted boundaries, holes and blue fringe; keep as inactive legacy rather than count it as an active style failure.

Source inspection shows a thin leader enclosed in an unusually broad blue/lavender cutout with a crisp noisy outline; the halo reads as a luminous sticker against matte skies. Replace with a finer irregular desaturated off-white bolt and softly dispersed low-opacity atmospheric glow; register both frames together.

Weathered ochre highlands, gray stone ruins and hazed mountain tiers establish the regional matte-painting benchmark; daylight warmth is restrained.
Charcoal coastal landforms dissolve into warm ash haze; subdued sea reflections and tiny lava accents support the volcanic biome without a different rendering style.
Muted umber volcanic terrain, smoke layers and sparse orange heat accents share the dark fantasy material treatment and atmospheric depth.
Cold gray-blue sea and ruined silhouettes recede through horizon mist. Detailed foreground water remains consistent with the regional landscape family.
Dense olive canopy, weathered hanging foliage and blue-gray depth haze form a coherent dark forest matte painting.
Dark rough rock and timber frame cool hazed openings with small warm lamps; depth and subdued material values suit the same fantasy family.
Worn Gothic masonry, diffuse cool shafts and restrained amber lamps share the regional painterly realism; distant arches soften convincingly.
Cold snow and slate peaks use overlapping mist layers and a storm ceiling. Brighter snow is intentional biome value design, with no cartoon or neon treatment.
Cold blue ice, gray ruined shores and hazed snow peaks match the winter biome. Cyan ice is the strongest natural color accent in this group but remains material-based, not emissive UI light.

recommendedChanges: Repaint batch-01 daylight sky toward muted overcast daylight while preserving composition; avoid applying one dark tint to every biome.
Replace both lightning frames as one registered effect with a fine off-white leader and diffuse restrained glow.
Keep fog-wisps disabled and explicitly labeled legacy; retain neutral vector fog as the main field.
Retain day/night and biome palette differences. Filters, particles and diffuse fog are functional vector overlays and need not imitate detailed brushwork.
evidence: All 12 unique sky/backdrop PNGs viewed individually at native dimensions.
Both lightning PNGs and fog/fog-wisps.png viewed individually.
scopeNotes: Approval is visual style approval only, not production registration, alpha cleanup or camera-safe coverage.
Lightning frame canvas mismatch remains a technical issue in addition to halo style.
